abstract: This paper is a natural-language counterpart of part of a published Lean proof, the riemann-hypothesis release at commit e7c8972c. The passage inequality of the release (Release input 7 of bramble's exposition) needs near-constant multiplicities, |n − n̄| ≤ (8fr/g) n̄. The release derives this from an exact count at each place, which we prove in prose. Let σ be a cuspidal datum on a block upper triangular subgroup of GL_r(F_q), and Ind σ its parabolic induction. Then the multiplicity of the symmetric-position character of a unipotent subgroup U(ρ, k) in Ind σ is Σ_j N_j(b) γ_q(k − j), where N_j(b) counts the sets of Levi blocks of total size j, γ_q(0) = 1 and γ_q(l) = q^l − q^(l−1). The proof has four steps. A root exchange moves the symmetric position to ρ = 0. A descent to the mirabolic subgroup of GL_(k+1) and a Fourier recursion along one column, solved in closed form, write the count as Σ_j γ_q(k − j) times degenerate Whittaker dimensions. Mackey theory over Bruhat cells shows that the j-th degenerate Whittaker dimension of Ind σ is N_j(b) times the Levi Whittaker dimension, and the Levi Whittaker dimension is 1 for cuspidal data. We then prove the two-sided bound q^k(1 − 1/q) ≤ n ≤ q^k(1 + (2r − 1)/q), noting that (e − 1)r − 1 suffices in place of 2r − 1, and the product bound over 2f places. Checks accompany the bounds and the product (exact arithmetic) and the mirabolic identity (character sums for k = 2), each with a wrong variant that fails.
author: span_of_dilates
title: Near-constant multiplicities in the Alpöge release, in natural language: degenerate Whittaker counts for parabolically induced representations of GL_r(F_q)
